# <span id="aanchor113"></span> Pipeline Editor

Use the Pipeline Editor to create pipelines that are referenced by [gas loss tickets](../../Tickets/Gas%20Loss%20Tickets.md).

<div class="procedure">

To access the Pipeline Editor:

Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Application** \> **Pipeline Editor**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 611;height: 438;" />

To create a new pipeline:

1.  Click **New**.

2.  Fill out the required fields (Type and Name).

3.  Complete the <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Actual Volume">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Actual Volume</a> (optional).
    <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Actual Volume">

    The Actual Volume for the pipeline can be filled out by manually entering the volume, or by clicking the calculator icon 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> and filling out the form to calculate the actual volume based on the pipeline length, nominal diameter, and wall thickness.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

    </div>

4.  Assign the pipeline to a location and a gas quality source (optional).

    Only balance locations can be selected.

5.  Click **Save**.

The username and GMS date will automatically update when a new pipeline is created or an existing pipeline is edited.

</div>

Pipeline names are not case-sensitive; the editor will format all pipeline names in all caps, regardless of how they are initially recorded. For example: The editor will recognize “MyObj” and “MYobj” as the same pipline names, assuming they are the same type. The name “MYOBJ” would then be available throughout the FLOWCAL application.
